video.title: Fantasy Basketball Punting: Not as Complicated as You Think

summary: Josh Lloyd explains punting in 9-category leagues. He defines it as ignoring a category to concentrate your resources, not as trying to be bad in that category. He covers how categories correlate, why punt-specific rankings can mislead, and why you should still draft guards early when you punt a guard stat. He calls first and second round "pairing" nonsense: what matters is value and a sensible 7 or 8 man core. He goes through Yahoo's top 12 ranked players, lists each one's weakest categories, and names possible round two partners. He closes with a mailbag answer: there are no rigid stat targets by round, and late picks should be upside flyers.

rules.text: Punting does not apply in points leagues. It is only for category leagues.
rules.quote: Punting is not a thing in points leagues. I've had many people over the years ask me that.

rules.text: Punting means ignoring one or more categories and acting as if they do not exist.
rules.quote: Punting is ignoring a category/categories. That's all. It's just ignoring a

rules.text: Fantasy value is finite. Spreading it over fewer categories raises your strength in each one, so punting simplifies decisions.
rules.quote: You have a finite amount of value that's sitting around in a fantasy league. So if you can pump it

rules.text: Punting is not trying to be bad. You target the other categories and accept whatever happens in the punted one. You can still win it sometimes.
rules.quote: You're not trying to make the category bad. You can punt a category, turnovers, for example, and you can win them.

rules.text: Do not fill your team with bad free throw players after taking Giannis. Your targets are still every player.
rules.quote: You do not need to accumulate all bad free throw centers with Giannis. If you get a player with good free throws, that's okay.

rules.text: Head-to-head playoffs need only 5 category wins, so even balanced teams end up punting something in the playoffs.
rules.quote: in the head-to-head playoffs? You've got to win five. So, how do you win five? Well, by not paying as much attention

rules.text: Punting is not the only way to win. You win fantasy with big value picks and smart waiver moves.
rules.quote: the way to win fantasy is big value picks and smart wave wire moves.

rules.text: Lloyd ignores turnovers in every head-to-head league.
rules.quote: This is how I approach every head league. I don't even care that turnovers exist.

rules.text: Watch category correlations. High assists go with high turnovers. Low turnovers go with low points and assists. High blocks go with high rebounds and FG%.
rules.quote: a player that gets high assists will get high turnovers. A player that has low turnovers will have low points and low assists.

rules.text: If you chase low-block players when punting blocks, your rebounds and FG% will suffer too.
rules.quote: that almost assuredly means your rebounds are going to be below par and you're going to struggle in field goal percentage.

rules.text: When you punt assists, check your threes, steals and FT%, because low-assist players often struggle there. Punting assists also brings turnovers down automatically.
rules.quote: am I getting enough threes? Are my steals okay? What's my free throw percentage looking like?

rules.text: Punt rankings lie, because they remove only your weak category and not everyone else's. Lloyd's DURANT ranking tries to correct for this.
rules.quote: What if you take the other person's worst category out, where do they go? And that's what Durant

rules.text: Do not avoid the punted category's player types. If you punt a guard stat (for example FT% with Giannis), draft guards in two of the next three rounds. Otherwise you slide into a 4 or 5 category punt.
rules.quote: If you're punting assists and guard stats, free throw percentage, for example, with Giannis, draft guards in round two and three

rules.text: You can change your punt at any time: mid draft, mid season or mid week.
rules.quote: you can change your punt mid draft, mid-season, midweek, whenever.

rules.text: First and second round pairing is nonsense. Any sensible first round pick plus a second round value can win. You only go wrong by reaching for a lesser player.
rules.quote: second round player in round two. Guess what? You're on the way. You're going to win.

rules.text: What matters is your 7 or 8 man core, not the two-player pair.
rules.quote: What is important is what is your seven or eightman core. That is what is important

rules.text: Treat best player available as a group of roughly equal options and take one of them. There is no single true best option.
rules.quote: There might be six different guys to pick from and generally if you're okay in that area, take one

rules.text: FG% and FT% vary a lot game to game, so punting one of them works well in head-to-head.
rules.quote: So, the idea of punting a variable category is pretty useful in a head-to-head format.

rules.text: Threes are easy to find on the waiver wire.
rules.quote: So now you're in a threes hole but we also know we can get threes off the wire.

rules.text: Points, assists and FT% are the scarcest categories later in drafts. If you don't get them early, you can just punt them.
rules.quote: Points become the hardest. They are the most scarce. assists, free throw percentage, they're the most scarce categories.

rules.text: Assists, rebounds and points are the most stable categories year to year and game to game.
rules.quote: that's useful in fantasy because they are the most stable categories year on year and game by game

rules.text: Stay flexible in drafts. If someone takes your target, take the next player rather than locking into a planned pair.
rules.quote: I just grab the next guy and we'll be fine. We'll figure it out. Be malleable. Be flexible.

rules.text: Do not push up players who gain value in punt rankings, such as bad FT% players, just to secure them.
rules.quote: doesn't mean you need to push him up because I got to secure all the bad free throw guys. You don't.

rules.text: Your first four picks and then your first eight picks need to make sense together.
rules.quote: is your first four picks and then your first eight picks. They have to make sense.

rules.text: First round players all have high turnovers, because turnovers are a third of the usage formula.
rules.quote: The first round of players all have bad turnovers. Giannis might have more than somebody, but it's not that big of a deal.

rules.text: Use at least three of your last four picks on upside flyers who could beat their draft spot by 40 to 50 places.
rules.quote: What I want to do in the last four rounds in at least three of them is take upside flyers.

rules.text: Don't set rigid stat or position targets by round. Plans break once picks start, especially in auctions. Fill positions, and get the early-scarce stats only if you want them.
rules.quote: no matter what draft you're in, go doubly for auction. As soon as something happens in a draft, your plan's gone.
